rv.q: We are once again invited to blow up balloons for the wedding between King Mark (Edward Rowe) and Yseult (Nandi Bhebhe) while her lover, Tristan (John Leader), simmers with secret passion in the wings. Well, I suppose some things just never get old.

Tristan, played by an engaging John Leader , is a young Frenchman visiting Cornwall who slays Irish invader Morholt (hilarious Tom Fox with superb comic timing). He's sent to bring Morholt's sister, Yseult (triple-threat Nandi Bhebhe ), back to be Cornish King Mark's (commanding Edward Rowe ) queen.

Twenty years after it first premiered, Emma Rice’s Tristan & Yseult still feels like one of the defining pieces of British theatre this century. Alongside her A Midsummer Night’s Dream , it remains the clearest example of what makes Rice such a distinctive theatre-maker.
